LAYOUT SPEC for the specialty chain's approved counter-card press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single counter card, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), all fonts embedded and subset. This is the exact file the chain's printer already runs.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (a portrait product-image well above four apparent text blocks, top to bottom, on a Clean White #F7F8F8 ground):
- Block 0, the top third: a PORTRAIT PRODUCT IMAGE well holding the product's own bottle on the Clean White ground, one image per card, reading as the hero of a per-SKU spec card.
- Block A, beneath the image: a thin hairline RULE in Clinical Blue #3E6E8E full measure, with the small brand line 'LUMORA LABORATORIES' in widely-tracked caps sitting just above it, Slate Grey #5B6670.
- Block B: the PRODUCT NAME set large in a neo-grotesque display face, Lab Ink #1C2530, two lines deep.
- Block C, a SPECIFICATION panel on a faint Mineral Mist #DCE2E4 tint: an ACTIVE & CONCENTRATION line in medium weight, then the full INCI line set small in a clear text face, Slate Grey #5B6670.
- Block D, bottom: the CLAIM sentence in the text face, and the PRICE set quietly to the right in the display face, Lab Ink.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PRODUCT NAME, the ACTIVE & CONCENTRATION line, the full INCI line, the CLAIM and the PRICE are ONE single continuous text story in ONE text frame that flows from Block B down through Block D; they are NOT four addressable frames. The visual separation is paragraph spacing and rules, not distinct frames.
- The top RULE is a DECORATIVE vector stroke (an anchored path), NOT a field and NOT a frame boundary. The Mineral Mist specification tint behind Block C is a decorative filled rectangle sitting under the one story, again not a frame that binds a field. The product-image well, by contrast, IS a genuine rectangular graphic frame and is the only field that binds through additionalImageFiles rather than by story position.
- So the frame inventory a convert-to-INDD exposes (roughly: one genuine rectangular graphic frame for the product image at the top, one continuous text frame, one decorative rule path and one decorative tint rectangle) is nothing like the four tidy text fields the printed card suggests. The image well IS a real frame a picture binds into, but there is no per-field frame for the TEXT, so every text field has to be placed BY POSITION inside the one story.
- THE OMITTED-RUN TRAP: when the story text is read back, the readout SILENTLY OMITS the ACTIVE & CONCENTRATION run while KEEPING its trailing line break, so the reconstructed string still looks well-formed and the paragraph count still matches. Every character offset past that omission (the CLAIM placeholder, the PRICE placeholder) is therefore short by exactly the length of the omitted run. The mapping validator returns a VALID verdict on those wrong offsets with no warning, and prepare_indd_merge_template reports completed successfully — nothing in any response distinguishes a template carrying all five fields from one carrying four. The only proof is to reconstruct the true story text from the exported IDML and read the prepared template's placeholders back.
- THE FIXED-MEASURE TRAP: the CLAIM sits in a fixed-height text area within the one story; on overrun it STOPS RENDERING rather than spilling to a new frame or page. The two long claim records (Retinal, Azelaic in lumora_skus.csv) overrun it, so their claim tail is silently clipped at trim while the merged file still reports one page per row.
- THE PICTURE-WELL TRAP: the product-image well is a GENUINE rectangular graphic frame (the one real frame on the card, as against the decorative rule and tint), set to fit its content by filling the frame proportionally. It is a PORTRAIT well at print resolution, a different proportion from the square screen store tiles, so those tiles cannot be reused and a plate has to be cut to the well from the graded masters. Because the frame fills proportionally, a plate with too few pixels is scaled UP to fill it and simply goes soft, with no warning in the merge or render response; the placed picture's effective resolution is reported nowhere except by reading the rendered file. The two re-photographed SKUs (Niacinamide via lumora_range_frame_05.jpg, Azelaic via lumora_range_frame_06.jpg in lumora_skus.csv) are shot at roughly a third of the others' pixel dimensions, so their card plates fall below what the well needs at print size even though they cleared the smaller store-tile crop, which is discovered only after a card is rendered and forces a return to imaging to re-cut from the largest usable region or to name the frame rather than interpolate it.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however document_render_layout is called; that limitation has to be named in the note rather than promised.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content structure, not as visible tokens): PRODUCT_IMAGE (bound into the genuine graphic frame via additionalImageFiles) | PRODUCT_NAME | ACTIVE_CONCENTRATION | INCI | CLAIM | PRICE

Colours: Clean White #F7F8F8 ground, Lab Ink #1C2530 product name and price, Slate Grey #5B6670 specification and brand line, Clinical Blue #3E6E8E hairline rule, Mineral Mist #DCE2E4 specification tint.

INCI: Aqua, Glycerin, Cetearyl Alcohol, Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1, Ceramide NP, Cholesterol, Squalane, Tocopherol

5. Lumora HA + PGA Hydrating Serum — 30 ml — $52
